key_insight: Instead of prompting a frozen LLM, train the model at test time with reinforcement learning so it adapts to the specific test problem and actively discovers a single best (potentially state‑of‑the‑art) solution.
problem_solved: Overcomes limitations of test‑time prompting and static models by enabling continual, instance‑specific learning aimed at producing one excellent solution for a scientific problem rather than many good solutions on average.
method: Run reinforcement learning during inference so the LLM updates from experience specific to the test instance (test‑time continual learning).
Optimize for a single high‑quality solution using episode‑level rewards and search-focused update rules, contrasting with prompting a frozen model.
Maintain practical safeguards (e.g., constrained updates or selective replay) to keep adaptation focused and stable while searching for a new best answer.
impact: Enables models to actively discover stronger, instance‑specific solutions and potentially push new state‑of‑the‑art results on scientific problems; useful for researchers and practitioners who need a single optimal result rather than averaged performance.
visual_elements: Side‑by‑side diagram: frozen prompting (no updates) vs test‑time RL (model updates during inference).
Flowchart of the test‑time RL loop: propose → evaluate → receive reward → update → repeat.
Performance curve showing test‑time RL discovering a new peak (SOTA) compared to baseline prompting.
Icon set: magnifying glass (discovery), lightning bolt (fast adaptation), target (single optimal solution).
paper_title: Learning to Discover at Test Time
paper_authors: Mert Yuksekgonul, Daniel Koceja, Xinhao Li, Federico Bianchi, Jed McCaleb
